core.title: Ship a route-control runner with its user/system-flow-resolution entry point when the journey map declares flow router routes
core.given: The consumer's composition root declares, in its action-to-route mapping (the journey map), at least one flow router route - a guarded-route value rather than a direct user/system flow reference
core.when: the consumer is changed or checked (any file, whenever the route was added)
core.then: Ship a route-control runner as a scanned source file in the tree the profile designates for it, exposing the user/system-flow-resolution entry point.
prefer: Ship one runner component whose construction accepts a reference to the route definitions and whose entry point accepts the action, its inputs and optional state, and returns a resolution.
The entry point evaluates guarded routes, resolves exactly one admissible user/system flow, then delegates execution to the user/system flow runner.
avoid: Flow router routes in the journey map with no route-control runner at all.
A route-control runner without the user/system-flow-resolution entry point.
A runner outside the designated tree, or present only in excluded generated/vendored trees (never scanned).
unless: Pure direct-train consumer: no flow router route in the journey map and no route-control runner.
core.why: A flow router is executable only as a route-control component: its entry point evaluates guarded routes and picks one admissible user/system flow before delegation, so without it declared routes cannot run.
evidence: If any journey-map value in the composition root is a flow router route, a route-control runner exists in a scanned source file of the designated tree and declares the user/system-flow-resolution entry point.
verification: Standing repository-state check: evaluated on the current repository state, not only on newly added routes, and it applies whichever file changed.

Flag when a flow router route is declared in the journey map but no route-control runner is shipped in the designated tree, or the runner lacks the user/system-flow-resolution entry point; compliance is shown by the stack's check for this rule reporting no finding.

An eligible runner is a scanned source file of the tree the profile designates for it: the profile supplies the journey-map idiom, the runner component and its tree, the scanned source file suffix and the excluded trees; which files are inspected and how the journey map, the runner and the entry point are recognized is the per-stack detector's concern.
Never scan the profile's excluded generated/vendored trees; a runner found only there does not satisfy the rule.
Do not flag a pure direct-train consumer: no flow router route in the journey map and no route-control runner.
Severity 4, disposition strict: a finding is not suppressible and fails CI.

fires: The journey map currently contains a flow router route and no route-control runner exists in the designated tree - including a pre-existing violation and a change touching only the composition root.
A flow router route is declared, a route-control runner exists, but it exposes no user/system-flow-resolution entry point.
A change introduces a new flow router route into the journey map.
A flow router route is declared and the only route-control runner lives in an excluded generated/vendored tree: excluded files never count as an eligible runner, so the rule still fires.
doesNotFire: A pure direct-train consumer: every journey-map value is a direct user/system flow reference and no route-control runner exists.

Scan exclusion: files in the profile's excluded generated/vendored trees are never scanned and never count as an eligible runner (this does not exempt a declared flow router route that lacks an eligible runner).

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the composition root lives; the file whose journey map declares the routes.
The composition root's action-to-route mapping construct (the journey map) itself; its placement is given by roles.composition_root.path.
How a journey-map value that routes through a flow router (a guarded route) is distinguished from a direct user/system flow reference.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a JOURNEY_MAP value that is an {flowRouterId, path} route object (flow router route), vs a direct userSystemFlowId string (direct user/system flow)

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's route-control component and the tree in which it must be shipped; the eligible files of that tree are its scanned source files (their suffix is suffix.source).
profileRequirements.bunValue: a `class FlowRouterRunner` under `src/user-system-flows/**`; the route-control component that selects one admissible user/system flow and delegates execution to FlowRunner

profileRequirements.meaning: The runner's entry point that evaluates guarded routes and resolves exactly one admissible user/system flow before delegation.
The file suffix of scanned production source; an eligible runner is a scanned source file of the designated tree.
Generated/vendored trees the check never scans; a runner found only there is not an eligible runner.

neutralityNotes: ATDD domain vocabulary (journey map, flow router, flow router route, user/system flow, user/system flow runner) is kept in the core: these are approach-level concepts, and the urn group already recognizes user/system flow and journey as artifact kinds. Placement of the journey map comes from the existing roles.composition_root.path key and the scanned source-file restriction from the existing suffix.source key, combined in core:verification with the designated runner tree; only the mapping construct, its value taxonomy, the runner component/tree and the entry point needed proposed idiom keys. core:prefer[0] adds no guidance beyond the Bun example: it neutralizes only its shape (construction accepts a reference to the route definitions; the entry point takes the action, its inputs and optional state and returns a resolution), and core:prefer[1] carries the resolve-then-delegate semantics that bun.json states explicitly. Detector, family and finding ids of this rule, the regex-over-source mechanism, the language-scoping activation fact, the concrete path globs and the code example are bunOnly. Per-rule severity 4 and strict disposition are kept in core:verification, and the exclusion deference (never scan the profile's excluded trees; a runner only there is ineligible) is preserved there rather than in the profile.
